title: The German version of the Young Person‘s Clinical Outcomes in Routine Evaluation (YP-CORE) questionnaire: Translation and evaluation of psychometric properties in clinical and non-clinical samples
summary: The Young Person’s Clinical Outcomes in Routine Evaluation (YP-CORE) is a brief questionnaire designed to help adolescents aged 11 to 18 self-assess their psychological distress using just ten items. Its free availability and user-friendly format have made it a widely used tool in several countries, particularly within psychological services for young people. It is especially well suited for monitoring and evaluating treatment progress. Until recently, there was no officially approved German version of the YP-CORE questionnaire. The aim of this study is to translate the original English version into German and to examine the practical suitability of this version. Between January and May 2025, a German version was developed using a recognized, multi-step translation procedure. To evaluate the questionnaire scientifically, data collection is now planned at secondary schools and university outpatient clinics for children and adolescents across German-speaking regions.
conditions: To examine the psychometric properties of the German version of the YP-CORE, data will be collected from both clinical samples (across different diagnoses) and non-clinical samples.

interventions.name: Non-clinical sample: Test-retest assessments at secondary schools of different types in German-speaking regions
Clinical sample: Repeated outcome measurements over the course of treatment in university outpatient clinics for child and adolescent psychotherapy in German-speaking regions

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- age between 11 and 18 years

Non-clinical sample: Signed consent forms for participation as well as for the collection and processing of data must be provided (for participants under the age of 15, the signature of a legal guardian is additionally required).

Clinical sample: A signed consent form for psychotherapeutic treatment must be provided, which also includes consent for the scientific use of questionnaire data and other health-related data in anonymized form (for patients under the age of 15, the signature of a legal guardian is additionally required).
Exclusion criteria:
- current use of professional mental health services (psychotherapeutic or psychiatric treatment) or actively seeking such support (applies only to non-clinical samples)
- insufficient german language skills
